config.title: Generic List<T>

intro.title: Generic List<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Angular component that displays a list of items of any type, such as a list of users, products, or tasks. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics, specifically the `List<T>` pattern, to create flexible and type-safe components. The main technologies involved are Angular components and TypeScript's generic type parameters. By the end, you'll understand how to write components that work with different data types while maintaining full type checking and IntelliSense support.
intro.usecase: Generic List<T> is a foundational pattern for building reusable, type-safe data components in Angular applications. You'll use it to create dynamic data tables in admin dashboards, where each column can display different data types like strings, numbers, or dates while maintaining strict type checking. It's also essential for building filterable product catalogs in e-commerce sites, where the same list component can render products, categories, or user reviews without code duplication. This approach ensures your UI components are flexible, maintainable, and scalable across different data models.

objectives: Implement a generic List<T> component with type parameter T
Initialize a generic list with different data types (string, number, custom object)
Render a generic list in the template using Angular's structural directives
Configure input properties to pass typed data to the generic component
Apply type safety by restricting list operations to the specified generic type
Manipulate list items through typed methods like add, remove, and filter
Integrate the generic List<T> component into a parent component with proper data binding

steps.title: Define items input property with generic type
steps.instruction: Inside the GenericListComponent class, add an @Input() property named 'items' with the type T[] to accept an array of generic items.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator from Angular/core. The property should be typed as T[] to match the component's generic type parameter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Input property with generic type
@Input() data: T[] = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed input property that can receive an array of any type.
successCriteria: The GenericListComponent class contains an @Input() items property with type T[].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the @Input() decorator and typed the property as T[].

steps.title: Define displayProperty input for dynamic property access
steps.instruction: Add an @Input() property named displayProperty to your GenericListComponent class. This property should have the type 'keyof T' to specify which property of the generic items to display.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator before the property declaration. The type 'keyof T' ensures the property name is valid for the generic type T.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a displayProperty input that accepts a string key of the generic type T, enabling dynamic property access for display.
successCriteria: The GenericListComponent class contains an @Input() property named displayProperty with type 'keyof T'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: In the template of your GenericListComponent, add the *ngFor directive to iterate over the items array and display each item's name property.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let item of items" on a div or list item element, then display {{ item.name }} inside.

// Similar: using *ngFor in Angular
  • {{ product.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a structural directive that iterates through the items array and displays each item's name.
successCriteria: The template contains *ngFor="let item of items" and displays {{ item.name }}.

steps.title: Use component in AppComponent with typed data
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add the <app-generic-list> component with [items] bound to sampleItems and [displayProperty] bound to 'name'.
steps.hint: Use property binding syntax with square brackets to pass data to the component inputs.

<app-user-list [users]="userArray" [displayField]="'email'"></app-user-list>
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent template will contain the generic list component with properly bound inputs using the sample data.
